name: sync
applies_to: two systems that share the same data
each_direction: Which details should go from {from} to {to}?
When someone adds a record in {from}, should it also appear in {to}?
When someone deletes a record in {from}, what should happen in {to}?
If a change fails to reach {to}, who should be told?
When a change from {from} shows in {to}, whose name should {to} show?
If {to} receives a value it does not allow, should it reject it, accept it, or flag it for review?
How soon must a change in {from} show in {to}?
Which time zone decides the dates sent to {to}?
once: Who on the customer's side approves giving us access to their data?
When the same record changes in {A} and in {B} before they sync, which change should win?
Should the customer see when that happens?
What should a person see when a change fails to sync?
Can someone retry a change that failed to sync?
Can people see whether a record is synced, waiting or failed?
When sync is first turned on, a record may exist in both places with different details. Which version should we keep?
Does anything about how data moves between {A} and {B} today need to change?
If many records change or are deleted at once, should sync pause for someone to approve it?
If a bad sync overwrites good data, must a customer be able to undo it?
Must there be a history of what each sync changed?
Who decides which details sync: the customer or us?
If either system rebuilds its data and record IDs change, how should records be matched again?
If the account that connects {A} and {B} is replaced, what should happen to changes already made?
